thread:
noah: Heads up — provisioning backlog in us-west1 for the last ~2h. GPUs queuing because nodes are stuck in 'drain' due to local-disk iops saturation. Looks like janitor skipped a bunch of tiny temp files and left a huge inode churn. Anyone seen this pattern?

julia: saw the same. iostat shows insane avgqu-sz on /dev/nvme0n1, cpuload fine. small random writes dominating.

raj: there was a janitor rollout at 02:10 UTC (rollback attempted at 03:05). rollback log showed "skiplist mismatch" on gnode-144. Might be related.

noah: exact. gnode-144/145/148 are the top offenders, ~9000 small files each. provisioning tried to attach GPUs and timed out while waiting on fsyncs.

julia: quick repro iostat snippet i ran:
```
Device        r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1     102.4  3400.1  512.3  1284.1  35.2   1.20  98.4
```

ek: thanks — I think this is the skiplist heartbeat race we discussed earlier but hitting a pathologic case: janitor walker yields many tiny delete ops, the GC backoff doesn't coalesce, and the fsync storm thrashes nvme. patch we shipped reduced batch size which made it worse under this workload.

noah: interesting, reduced batch made it worse? I thought smaller batches reduce per-transaction latency.

ek: in steady state yes, but here the walker tries to keep many in-flight deletions; smaller batches increase number of fsync windows and prevent the kernel from merging bio requests. Bigger batches + paced flush reduces syscalls and gives SSD controller better write coalescing.

sre-oncall: mitigation suggestion: 1) set JANITOR_COALESCE=true and bump JANITOR_BATCH=1024 on affected AZs, 2) temporarily taint nodes to avoid provisioning until scrub finishes, 3) run a targeted forced scrub on gnode-144/145.

raj: can we do (2) quickly? provisioning backlog is blocking a customer job.

noah: I'll taint the three nodes now and scale the pool manually. Doing: `kubectl taint nodes gnode-144 node.kubernetes.io/provisioning-block=true:NoSchedule`

ops-bot: [alert] autoscaler paused for pool-worker-us-west1 for 18m by noah — reason: local-nvme-iops-surge

julia: for forced scrub, command I ran worked: `/usr/local/bin/janitor --zone us-west1 --node gnode-144 --force-clean --max-delete 20000` — note: it spikes iops briefly then back off. use during maintenance window.

ek: I'll prepare a rollbackable config change and a Canary: set COALESCE=true + BATCH=1024 on 5 canary nodes first, watch iostat and provision queue. If stable, roll to AZ.

sre-oncall: timeline?

ek: starting canary in 10m, monitor for 30m. if avgq < 5 and %util < 80, proceed.

noah: and follow-up: create an alert that triggers when "small-write-ratio" > 70% AND avgqu-sz > 10 for >5m. current alerts too coarse.

raj: noted. I'll own the alert PR.

julia: postmortem checklist: include janitor batch heuristics, telemetry for small-file churn, and a runbook for taint + scrub.

noah: thanks all. ek — ping me once canary green and I'll untaint and resume provisioning. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [info] janitor-canary-deploy started by ek on 5 nodes — canary id c-2023-11-02-08

sre-oncall: good call on the alert. Also tagging storage-team for follow-up architecture changes.

noah: closing loop here — provisioning backlog cleared after forced scrub and canary roll; will open postmortem.
